in_arabic.name: براءة
in_arabic.meaning: البراءة من اللوم أو العيب أو الإثم
in_arabic.long_meaning: براءة هو اسم مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ب ر ء' والذي يعني التخلص من اللوم أو العيب أو الإثم. ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة الأعراف الآية 168 'وَلَقَدْ بَرَأْنَا لَهُمُ الْأَرْضَ مُطَهَرَةً'. يرمز الاسم إلى النزاهة والشرف والابتعاد عن كل ما هو سيئ أو مذموم.

in_urdu.name: برات
in_urdu.meaning: بے داغ یا بے عیب ہونا
in_urdu.long_meaning: برات نام کی اصطلاح عربی جڑ 'ب ر ء' سے نکلی ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے بے داغ یا بے عیب ہونا۔ یہ نام اسلامی تقویم میں اہم سمجھا جاتا ہے کیونکہ یہ پاکیزگی اور صفائی کی علامت ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں میں اس کا استعمال روایتی ہے اور یہ نام نوجوانوں میں مقبول ہے۔

in_hindi.name: बरात
in_hindi.long_meaning: बरात नाम की उत्पत्ति अरबी मूल 'ब र ء' से हुई है, जिसका अर्थ है निर्दोष या दोषरहित होना। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में महत्वपूर्ण माना जाता है और यह पवित्रता और शुद्धता का प्रतीक है। इस नाम का उपयोग पारंपरिक है और युवा पीढ़ी में लोकप्रिय है।

in_pashto.name: برات
in_pashto.meaning: د بې ګناهۍ یا بې عیبۍ مانا
in_pashto.long_meaning: برات د عربي ريښو 'ب ر ء' څخه اخیستل شوی دی، کوم چې د بې ګناهۍ یا بې عیبۍ معنی لري. دا نوم د افغان او پښتون دودیزو ټولنو کې کارول کیږي او پاکۍ او سادگۍ ته اشاره کوي. په پښتنو کې دا نوم د احترام وړ دی او د نوي زېږيدونکو ماشومانو لپاره انتخابیږي.

in_english.name: Baraat
in_english.meaning: innocence, guiltlessness, or being free from blame
in_english.long_meaning: Baraat originates from the Arabic root 'ب ر ء' (bara'a), meaning to disengage, free oneself, or be absolved. It signifies innocence, guiltlessness, or being free from blame. Referenced in the Quran (Surah Al-A'raf, Verse 168), it connotes purity and moral integrity. Historically, it has been used across Islamic cultures, symbolizing honor and righteousness.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Baraat" in Islam holds significant cultural importance, as it refers to one who performs a great act or a pilgrimage to the holy city of Makkah. Baraat is the name given to pilgrims who have completed their Hajj (the Islamic pilgrimage) or Umrah (a lesser pilgrimage) to the holy mosque in Mecca. During these pilgrimages, Muslims wear special clothing and follow a series of rituals, which includes walking seven times around the Kaaba, offering prayers, and symbolically casting stones at pillars representing Satan. The cultural significance of Baraat can be seen in the immense sense of fulfillment and joy experienced by Muslims after performing their pilgrimages, and the way these journeys often bring people from different parts of the world together in a shared spiritual experience.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, the term "Baraat" signifies the concept of delivering from sin and providing a pathway to divine forgiveness. It is believed that carrying out the pilgrimage to Mecca, known as the Hajj, cleanses a Muslim's soul from past sins and helps them reconnect with their faith. This purified state is referred to as a state of Ihram, or consecration, during which Muslims refrain from engaging in various worldly activities. The spiritual significance of Baraat can be seen in its role as a reminder of the temporary nature of earthly life and the constant need for seeking forgiveness and closeness to God. It is also a testimony to the potential for spiritual transformation and the importance of making a daily effort to purify one's intentions, actions, and thoughts.
